source: ace-bank-ochem main 1639ba7, trap-families/families.json (Thomas approved 2026-11-17). Names and fixes only.

families.name: Judged the acid instead of its conjugate base
families.fix: To compare acids, remove the H and ask which anion is more stable; the more stable conjugate base belongs to the stronger acid.

families.name: Atom size vs electronegativity mixed up
families.fix: Down a column, size wins (HI is a stronger acid than HF); across a row, electronegativity wins (HF beats H2O beats NH3).

families.name: Missed (or overrated) the resonance
families.fix: Look for a lone pair, pi bond or charge next to a pi bond; delocalized charge is stabilized, and a lone pair tied up in resonance is less basic and less nucleophilic.

families.name: Induction misjudged (distance, or donor vs withdrawer)
families.fix: Electron-withdrawing groups (halogens, NO2, C=O) stabilize anions and raise acidity, more strongly the closer they sit; alkyl groups donate and do the opposite.

families.name: Hybridization or s-character misread
families.fix: Count electron domains (4 is sp3, 3 is sp2, 2 is sp); more s-character holds an anion closer, so sp C-H (pKa about 25) beats sp2 and sp3.

families.name: Leaned on sterics when another factor decides
families.fix: Use sterics only when charge, atom, resonance and induction are tied; it decides SN2 rates and bulky bases, rarely acidity rankings.

families.name: Acid-base direction or strength reversed (pKa, equilibrium, base strength)
families.fix: Lower pKa is the stronger acid, and an acid-base equilibrium favors the side with the weaker acid and weaker base (the higher pKa).

families.name: Tried SN2 at a blocked carbon (tertiary, neopentyl, aryl or vinyl)
families.fix: SN2 needs a clear backside: methyl and primary are fine, tertiary, neopentyl, aryl and vinyl halides never do SN2.

families.name: Conformation slip: chair axial/equatorial, Newman, or the anti-periplanar E2 rule
families.fix: Draw the chair or Newman: big groups go equatorial or anti, a ring flip swaps every axial and equatorial spot, and E2 needs the H and leaving group anti-periplanar (both axial in a ring).

families.name: Stereo outcome of the reaction wrong (syn vs anti, inversion vs racemic)
families.fix: Ask how the new bond forms: backside attack inverts, a flat intermediate gives racemic, bridged ions and epoxides add anti, and concerted reagents (OsO4, BH3, H2/Pd) add syn.

families.name: Wrong SN1/SN2/E1/E2 call (substrate, base, solvent, heat, Zaitsev vs Hofmann)
families.fix: Decide by substrate (methyl/primary SN2, tertiary SN1/E1/E2), then reagent (strong small nucleophile SN2, strong bulky base E2 Hofmann, weak nucleophile plus heat E1), then solvent (aprotic SN2, protic SN1).

families.name: Forgot the carbocation rearrangement (or shifted when none happens)
families.fix: Whenever a carbocation forms next to a more substituted carbon, check for a 1,2-hydride or methyl shift; concerted and bridged paths (SN2, E2, oxymercuration, FC acylation) never rearrange.

families.name: Picked the wrong nucleophile or electrophile (cross out the metal)
families.fix: Cross out the counter-ion: the electron-rich atom (lone pair or C-metal bond) attacks, and the electrophile is the carbon with the partial positive charge.

families.name: Markovnikov vs anti-Markovnikov flip (wrong carbon)
families.fix: Ionic HX, H3O+ and oxymercuration put the nucleophile on the more substituted carbon; hydroboration (and HBr with peroxide) put it on the less substituted one.

families.name: Radical vs ionic pathway mixed up (peroxide, NBS, light)
families.fix: Light, heat or peroxide means radicals: HBr with ROOR adds anti-Markovnikov (HBr only), and NBS substitutes the allylic or benzylic H instead of adding.

families.name: Leaving group misjudged (OH not activated, weak base leaves best)
families.fix: A good leaving group is a weak, stable base (I-, Br-, TsO-, H2O); OH, OR and NH2 must be protonated or converted (TsCl, PBr3, SOCl2) before they leave.

families.name: Energy diagram or rate misread (Ea, intermediate, rate step, kinetic vs thermodynamic)
families.fix: Peaks are transition states, valleys are intermediates, the highest peak sets the rate, and the lower-energy product is thermodynamic while the lower barrier product is kinetic.

families.name: Arrow or formal charge bookkeeping slip
families.fix: Arrows start at a lone pair or bond and point where the electrons go; recount formal charge (valence minus dots minus sticks) on every atom an arrow touches.

families.name: Redox ladder: oxidizer or reducer went too far or not far enough
families.fix: Count bonds to O: PCC stops a primary alcohol at the aldehyde and Jones goes to the acid; NaBH4 reduces only aldehydes and ketones while LiAlH4 also reduces esters, acids and amides.

families.name: Alkyne reagent swap (Lindlar vs Na/NH3, NaNH2, hydration)
families.fix: Lindlar gives the cis alkene, Na/NH3 the trans alkene, H2/Pd goes all the way to the alkane, and NaNH2 only deprotonates a terminal alkyne.

families.name: Alkene reagent route swapped (OsO4 vs epoxide, HX vs X2, ozonolysis workup)
families.fix: Match each alkene reagent to one product: HX adds H and X, X2 adds two X anti, OsO4 a syn diol, mCPBA then H3O+ an anti diol, and O3 cuts the C=C into two C=O (Zn/DMS aldehydes, H2O2 acids).

families.name: Grignard (or organolithium) killed by an acidic H, or wrong carbonyl target
families.fix: Grignards are strong bases first: any O-H, N-H or terminal alkyne H in the molecule quenches them; with esters they add twice to give a tertiary alcohol.

families.name: Climbed the carbonyl ladder (acid derivative reactivity order)
families.fix: Acyl substitution only goes downhill: acid chloride > anhydride > ester (acid) > amide, ranked by how weak a base the leaving group is.

families.name: Carbonyl addition product wrong (acetal, imine/enamine, Wittig, aldol/Claisen/Michael)
families.fix: Name the partner first: alcohols give acetals, primary amines imines, secondary amines enamines, ylides alkenes; an enolate adds 1,2 (aldol) or 1,4 (Michael) and esters give Claisen.

families.name: Directing effect swapped (ortho/para vs meta, activator vs deactivator)
families.fix: Lone-pair donors and alkyls direct ortho/para and activate; carbonyls, NO2, CN, SO3H and CF3 direct meta and deactivate; halogens deactivate but still direct ortho/para.

families.name: Aromaticity misjudged (Huckel count, lone pair in or out)
families.fix: Aromatic needs cyclic, planar, fully conjugated and 4n+2 pi electrons; count a lone pair only if that atom has no pi bond already in the ring.

families.name: Reagent role misremembered (what the reagent actually does)
families.fix: Write each reagent next to the bond it makes or breaks before reading the choices; if you cannot say what it does, it is the trap.

families.name: Naming slip: wrong chain, numbering or suffix
families.fix: Find the longest chain that holds the highest-priority group, number from the end that gives it the lowest locant, then list substituents alphabetically.

families.name: Miscounted stereocenters or stereoisomers
families.fix: A stereocenter needs four different groups (no sp2 or CH2 carbons); then count 2^n and subtract the meso forms.

families.name: Isomer relationship mixed up (enantiomer, diastereomer, meso, identical, constitutional)
families.fix: Check the formula and connectivity first, then flip every stereocenter: all flipped is enantiomer, some flipped is diastereomer, and an internal mirror plane makes it meso.

families.name: R/S or E/Z priority slip
families.fix: Rank by atomic number at the first point of difference, and if the lowest priority points at you, reverse the direction you read.

families.name: Missed the symmetry (equivalent H or C)
families.fix: Draw the mirror plane or rotation axis first; atoms that swap places under it give one signal.

families.name: Functional group misidentified (ester vs ketone vs aldehyde vs acid vs amide)
families.fix: Name what is bonded to the carbonyl carbon (H aldehyde, two C ketone, OH acid, OR ester, N amide) before using any rule that depends on the group.

families.name: Spectroscopy landmark misread (IR band, NMR shift, splitting, integration)
families.fix: Anchor on the landmarks first (IR 1700 C=O, broad 3300 O-H, 2200 triple bond; NMR 9-10 aldehyde, 10-12 acid, 6.5-8 aromatic), then use n+1 splitting and integration.

families.name: Polarity or IMF trend flipped (boiling point, solubility, dipole)
families.fix: Rank by intermolecular forces (H-bond > dipole > London), then by surface area: more H-bonding and more surface raise boiling point, and like dissolves like.

families.name: Lab technique step misjudged (TLC, extraction, recrystallization, distillation)
families.fix: Tie each step to one property: TLC and columns separate by polarity, extraction by charge (pKa vs the layer pH), recrystallization by hot-vs-cold solubility, distillation by boiling point.

families.name: Product bookkeeping slip: carbon count, ring size, or how many times it reacts
families.fix: Count carbons and rings in the start, the carbon-adding reagents and the product, and read the equivalents: excess reagent hits every reactive site, one equivalent hits the most reactive one.

families.name: Steps out of order or a step skipped (synthesis or mechanism)
families.fix: Work backward from the target one bond at a time, and check that each step leaves a group the next reagent can use (directors, protecting groups, oxidation level).

families.name: Arithmetic or ratio inverted (ee, rotation, pKa ratio)
families.fix: Write the formula before the numbers: ee = (major - minor) / total x 100, observed rotation = ee x specific rotation, and each pKa unit is a factor of 10.
